input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "invariant",
 "proof_obligation": "bridge",
 "diagnosis": "The loop invariant bound '0<i<=v.Length+1' is too weak: it allows i==v.Length+1, so min(v,i) and countMin(v,mini,i) in the other invariants are not well-defined (their preconditions require i<=v.Length), and at loop exit i>=v.Length together with i<=v.Length+1 does not give i==v.Length, so the postcondition c==countMin(v,min(v,v.Length),v.Length) cannot be derived. Tightening the bound to 0<i<=v.Length fixes well-formedness and the bridge to the postcondition."}
EOF
sed -i 's/invariant 0<i<= (v.Length) + 1/invariant 0<i<= v.Length/' program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.content: Dafny program verifier finished with 4 verified, 0 errors

content.text:
`program.dfy` now verifies: Dafny reports "4 verified, 0 errors".

**What was wrong:** the loop invariant at line 38, `invariant 0<i<= (v.Length) + 1`, had an upper bound that was off by one. It caused all three errors:
- **Lines 39–40:** the invariant allowed `i == v.Length+1`. That is outside the allowed range for `min(v,i)` (which requires `i<=v.Length`) and for `countMin(v,mini,i)` (which requires `0<=i<=v.Length`). So the other two invariants weren't well-defined.
- **Postcondition at line 30:** when the loop exits, Dafny knows `i >= v.Length` and `i <= v.Length+1`. That doesn't force `i == v.Length`, so the invariants couldn't be turned into `c==countMin(v,min(v,v.Length),v.Length)`.

**Fix:** I tightened the bound to `invariant 0<i<= v.Length`. The invariant still holds when the loop starts (`i = 1` and `v.Length > 0`), and each iteration keeps it true because the loop only runs while `i < v.Length`. At exit it now gives `i == v.Length`, so the postcondition follows. I didn't need to change any other line.

`diagnosis.json` was written before the edit, as `invariant` / `bridge`.
